title: Geometry-Centered 3D Latent World Models for Growing Surfaces
claim: A multi-stage latent model fuses partial sensors, allocates limited state to growing regions, and rolls dynamics forward, with physics guidance used only in training.
layout: Single wide row, left-to-right, four module panels plus training-only panel at right
description: A wide left-to-right pipeline diagram. At far left is a 3D growing surface colored blue (matured) to red (actively growing), feeding a pink box of image, mesh and point-cloud views linked by magenta correspondence lines. These produce a column of fused tokens. A green panel (Growth-Aware State Allocation) groups red growth-front, red-blue interface, blue mature scaffold and gray global-summary tokens, driven by an 'Activity Scoring' arrow. An orange panel (Action-Conditioned Dynamics) chains Front, Boundary, Scaffold and Global update blocks, conditioned on control action and time horizon inputs. A predicted-state token column leads to a Loss node. A vertical line divides Deployment from Training. The right side shows privileged physics, EMA tokenizer and GASA boxes, plus a later-time surface and an orange counterfactual result. A legend sits at lower left.
caption: FOLIAGE models growing surfaces by building a geometric state from partial sensors, allocating a fixed state budget according to estimated growth activity, and rolling the state forward under material-control actions. Privileged physical signals guide training only (not required at deployment).
abstract: Many physical systems do not merely move or deform; they grow, adding material and changing the geometry that a world model must represent. Existing world models are typically optimized for pixel prediction, reward prediction, or fixed-support physical dynamics, leaving open how to model systems whose underlying physical support expands over time and whose future morphology depends on hidden material response. We introduce FOLIAGE, a geometry-centered latent world model for growing surfaces. Within a fixed state budget, FOLIAGE represents mature regions as a compact scaffold while allocating higher-resolution state to regions predicted to drive near-future growth. This focuses representation and computation where new material and geometric change occur while retaining compact global context. FOLIAGE further separates observation, action, and privileged physics: heterogeneous RGB, point-cloud, and mesh observations are fused into a deployable geometric state; material controls condition the latent dynamics; and hidden physical energies guide training but are not required at deployment. To evaluate this setting, we introduce SURF-GARDEN and SURF-BENCH, providing controlled counterfactual branches, dense cross-modal correspondences, hidden physical signals, and stress tests for growing-geometry state learning. FOLIAGE reduces inverse-material error by $\approx40\%$ and 5-step mesh forecasting Chamfer error by $\approx30\%$ relative to strong baselines, while improving cross-modal retrieval by +14 mAP points. Stress tests show graceful degradation under sensor loss and correspondence corruption. On temporal 3D plant scans, FOLIAGE also improves passive future-geometry forecasting, while transfer experiments show that the learned geometry-centered state remains useful beyond the simulator.
